segments.t: We are in midtown Manhattan at Good Shepherd Services, which is a beneficiary of the Robinhood
Foundation.
Joining us right now in an exclusive interview is legendary investor Paul Tudor Jones.
Of course, he's the founder and chief investment officer of the Tudor Investment Corporation.
He's also, of course, the founder and board member of the Robinhood Foundation, which
is hosting its annual investor conference next week.
You got a huge lineup, and it's great to see you.
And by the way, great to be here at Good Shepherd Services, which is a foundation that
Robinhood has long supported.
We've supported them for over 30 years.
They're kind of like the Kobe or the shack of not-for-profits in New York City.
They serve 30,000 kids.
Just a spectacular organization.
I first met them, and it was run by Sister Paulette.
And if you met her, you would want to hug her.
She was just the most brilliant, loving, warm, human being.
And she said she's retired, but she's not.
She's still working and has new ideas.
And Michelle, who runs the place now, plays catch with her all the time.
So it's a great place.
And again, the best thing about this is this place, it believes so firmly as we do,
a child's circumstance does not determine their future.
I want to talk philanthropy in New York City and Robinhood and this conference as well.
But I want to talk markets, if you'd indulge me.
Because we have bank earnings coming out this morning.
But I was thinking back to a conversation that we had about a year ago, around this
same time.
And I had said something to the effect to you of where do you think we are in the market
cycle?
And you said something to the effect of maybe it's like 1999.
But remember that the market still went up another 40% after 1999.
So here we are a year later.
Where do you think we really are?
Well, it still feels like 1999, a two speed market.
